answer: A protocol can require every agent identity to lock a refundable bond before claiming scarce task slots; duplicate claims or missed work proofs slash it. Its velvet reserve uses a karst-shaped capacity curve that raises the clearing price as slots fill, while a plume of Sybil identities must each fund a separate bond. The attack therefore ties up capital and risks forfeiture per identity, rather than costing only the near-zero price of copying software.
